title: Explaining a Delay Without Making Excuses
scene: A task is taking longer than expected. You need to explain the delay clearly, show what you are doing about it, and give a realistic deadline without sounding defensive.
sceneJa: 予定より作業が遅れている。言い訳にせず、理由・現状・影響・期限まで整理して伝える。

chunks.ja: 更新作業にはかかっています

chunks.en: a little longer than I expected
chunks.ja: 予想していたより少し長く
なぜなら見つけたからです

chunks.en: a few inconsistencies in the data.
chunks.ja: データにいくつかの不整合を
自信を持てないものを
その数字をもう一度確認しています
レポートを完成させる前に
すでに終わっています
なので、これは〜とは考えていません
全体のスケジュールに影響する

chunks.en: I should be able to send you
chunks.ja: お送りできる見込みです

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: The update is taking / a little longer than I expected
The update / is taking a little / longer than I expected
The update is / taking a little longer / than I expected
questions.explanation: The first chunk introduces the situation, and the second gives the comparison: it is taking a little longer than expected.

questions.question: What does ‘Rather than sending something I’m not confident in’ mean?
options: Send it first and check it later
Choose another action instead of sending something uncertain
Send it because the speaker is confident
questions.explanation: ‘Rather than A’ sets up the action the speaker chooses not to take, followed by the preferred alternative.

questions.question: What does ‘by tomorrow morning’ mean?
questions.explanation: ‘By’ marks a deadline: the final version should be sent no later than tomorrow morning.

speak: Sound responsible rather than apologetic. State the delay calmly, explain the reason without becoming defensive, add reassurance at ‘Most of the work is already done,’ and make ‘by tomorrow morning’ clear and definite so the listener hears the deadline.
review: Previous flow: observation → possible explanation → caution → check → stronger conclusion. Today’s flow: delay → reason → choice → current status → impact → deadline. Good updates reduce uncertainty by answering what happened, why, what you are doing, whether it affects the wider plan, and when it will be ready.
